Sofia: FYI while validating zephyr-28k-int3 onboarding I hit a deterministic token split / off-by-one around token ~12048. Only happens with `--kv-prefetch=on` + `--rope-policy=phase-shear`. Repro steps below.

Sofia: Repro: `./ci_run --model zephyr-28k-int3 --quant=int3 --kv-prefetch=on --rope-policy=phase-shear --ctx=32768 --seed=42 --prompt=bench/long_loop.txt`

Sofia: Short log excerpt: 
```
[00:12:03] kv: window=131072 horizon=8192 prefetch_chunks=16
[00:12:03] pos=12048 phase_shear=0.99912 frac_accum=0.423981
[00:12:03] kv_write=12047 kv_read=12048 <-- expected read==write but observed shift when horizon boundary crossed
```

Liam: Hmm. Does it reproduce if you disable scheduling extrapolation? Try `--rope-policy=phase-shear --no-extrapolate`. Also, can you capture `KV_INDEX` and `ROPE_SCALE` dumps at the boundary?

Sofia: Good idea. Added `KV_INDEX_DUMP=1 ROPE_DUMP=/tmp/rope.json`. Will push dumps to trace id 1790001001.

bench-bot: Trace 1790001001 available: https://telemetry.internal/trace/1790001001 (ttl 7d)

Nadia: Quick hypothesis: phase-shear computes a per-pos multiplier that is non-monotonic across the chunk boundary because shear is applied piecewise per-chunk. Combined with int3 quant rounding to nearest 1/8, the mapped KV slot index can flip at boundary. That would look like a 1-token slip at predictable multiples of chunk size.

Rae: I saw similar earlier with magnet models but under a different name. Workaround we used then: enforce monotonic ROPE scale by post-processing the scale array with `scale[i] = min(scale[i], scale[i+1])` from high->low (i.e., clip uphill steps). Could try here and see if it stops the slip.

Sofia: Quick local test: patched runtime to clip scales monotically within each prefetch chunk. Re-ran single-thread reproducer, slip gone at 12048 but new slip at 16384 boundary. Looks like clipping delays the breakpoint rather than fixing root cause.

Liam: That suggests accumulation across prefetch horizon still problematic. Two vectors to explore: 1) change rounding semantics for computing kv_slot (bankers rounding / round-to-even) and 2) make prefetch reads use a stable reference mapping calculated with high-precision fixed point then truncated once per horizon.

Nadia: I prefer (2). Compute mapping as fixed-point 64-bit with a chosen scale_nbits (e.g., 2**20), store integer mapping per pos, and use the same mapping for read/write across all shards for that horizon window. Avoid recomputing per-shard where floating/quant differences could diverge.

Sofia: Implemented a quick proof-of-concept: `scale_fixed = (int64_t)(rope_scale * (1<<20))`, `kv_idx = (pos * scale_fixed) >> 20` and snap at horizon boundary. Local reproducible run passes for 12048 & 16384. Posting diffs to trace 1790001001/diffs_fixedpoint.txt

Rae: Nice. Can you run fuzzbench matrix: int3/int4, shear/linear, prefetch horizons 4k/8k/16k, and both fixedpoint vs current? If fixedpoint reduces diffs across the matrix it's a strong candidate for upstream change.

Sofia: Scheduling the matrix now. Bench matrix id: fuzz-1790002002. Will attach summary when done.

bench-bot: fuzz-1790002002 started: https://telemetry.internal/fuzz/fuzz-1790002002 (matrix: 24 runs)

Liam: One more note: if we change to fixedpoint mapping, we should audit perf (multiplication + shift) vs current float path. Likely negligible relative to token compute, but check on CPU-bound prefill paths. Add perf counters for mapping_time micros.

Sofia: Added `mapping_time_us` histograms to telemetry. First sweep indicates ~0.6us extra per token in prefill stage, acceptable for onboarding workloads.

Nadia: Also add unit tests that assert `kv_read`/`kv_write` parity across shard reorderings and after serialization/deserialization of mapping table. We caught one subtle endianness bug on s390 in a previous life.

Rae: I'll open a draft PR with the fixedpoint mapping + tests + opt-in feature flag `--rope-mapping=fixedpoint|float` so we can run internal canaries before defaulting. Tagging @infra-team for rollout notes.

Sofia: Thanks all. Prioritizing P2 for this model since it blocks onboarding and fuzzbench is green so far. Attaching traces and diffs in the telemetry links above. I'll post fuzz matrix results when complete. :thumbsup:
